e: Two men are seriously injured after an explosion at an oil refinery in Agioi Theodoroi.
The US and Greece agree on a coordinated security framework for counterterrorism information sharing among respective law enforcement agencies.
Greece repatriates the remains of Samuel of Bulgaria, which were previously stored at the Museum of Byzantine Culture in Thessaloniki, to Sofia.
Six people are killed when a three-story building collapses after an explosion in Plaka, Athens.
A cargo vessel catches fire off Mykonos, forcing the evacuation of all 29 people on board.
Neo-Nazi politician Ilias Kasidiaris is released from prison.
An F-4 Phantom II of the Hellenic Air Force crashes during an aerial show in Tanagra Air Base, killing the two pilots.
Greece and Israel sign a €3 billion weapons agreement.
A British couple on their honeymoon and their Greek pilot are killed in a helicopter crash on the island of Sifnos.
Mount Olympus is designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
A General Dynamics F-16 Fighting Falcon of the Hellenic Air Force crash-lands and catches fire at Zakynthos International Airport. The pilot is rescued.
A firebombing on the homes of New Democracy party members in Thessaloniki kills one person and injures three others.
Alexandros Giotopoulos, the head of the far-left militant group Revolutionary Organization 17 November, is released on parole after 23 years in prison.
Greece's Akylas finishes 10th at Eurovision 2026 in Austria with the single "Ferto".
A Ukrainian naval drone is discovered off Lefkada.
Four people are injured in separate shootings carried out by the same gunman in Athens.
The government announces a ban on people under 15 years old from accessing social media effective in 2027.

Prime minister Mitsotakis conducts a cabinet reshuffle amid criticism over the improper use of agrarian subsidies from the EU by MPs, resulting in the removal of Agriculture Minister Kostas Tsiaras, Civil Protection Minister Yiannis Kefalogiannis, and Deputy Health Minister Dimitris Vartzopoulos.
A Frontex patrol boat carrying the Estonian ambassador capsizes off Kastellorizo, injuring four people.
A magnitude 5.3 earthquake hits Epirus, damaging around 140 houses.
The government orders the deployment of two frigates and two F-16 fighter jets to Cyprus in response to Iranian drone strikes on the island amid the 2026 Iran war.
A boat carrying migrants capsizes off the coast of Kaloi Limenes, Crete, killing four passengers and leaving 30 others missing.
A mob attack on riot police results in 313 arrests following a raid at the Aristotle University of Thessaloniki.
A speedboat carrying migrants collides with a patrol vessel of the Hellenic Coast Guard off Chios, killing 15 people.
Five people are killed in an explosion at the Violanta biscuit factory near Trikala.
Two people are killed in separate storm-related incidents in Glyfada and Astros.

A court in Lesbos acquits 24 volunteer rescuers from the nonprofit Emergency Response Centre International, including Syrian swimmer Sarah Mardini, on charges of human trafficking over their efforts to rescue migrants arriving in Greece from Turkey.
A massive interference on aviation radio frequencies causes a total shutdown of Greek airspace, causing major disruptions nationwide.
